s: A company has a central data lake account. Data is stored in Amazon S3 and cataloged in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Analysts in three other AWS accounts query the data with Amazon Athena. Analysts must not see the columns that contain personal data (ssn and date_of_birth), and each analyst team must see only the rows for its own country. The data lake team wants to manage these permissions centrally without copying data. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Register the S3 locations with AWS Lake Formation. Create data filters that exclude the personal data columns and filter rows by country, and grant them to the consumer accounts (shared through AWS RAM). In each consumer account, create resource links and grant the analysts access.
Create a copy of each table without the personal data columns for each country, store the copies under separate S3 prefixes, and give each account access with S3 bucket policies.
Create Athena views in each consumer account that hide the personal data columns and filter by country, and tell the analysts to query only the views.
Use Amazon Macie to find the personal data columns and mask them automatically before the analysts run queries.

w.y: Lake Formation provides fine-grained access control on Data Catalog tables: data filters can include or exclude columns, filter rows with a PartiQL expression, or both (cell-level). Grants can be shared with other accounts through AWS RAM; consumers create resource links so Athena can query the shared tables, and Lake Formation enforces the filters at query time.

o.A: Correct. Central, fine-grained (column and row) permissions across accounts, with one copy of the data.
o.B: Copies multiply storage and pipeline work, drift out of date, and S3 policies cannot filter columns or rows inside a file.
o.C: The underlying tables remain readable, so the views are not a control; anyone can query the base table directly.
o.D: Macie discovers and reports sensitive data in S3. It does not mask data or enforce query permissions.

s: Cross-account data sharing in Lake Formation
